name.text: Calculating theoretical probability using the complement rule (at least one)

questiontext.text:
A high school in Kakamega is selecting students to represent them at the National Drama Festival. The drama club has {@num_actors@} actors and {@num_singers@} singers.

[[jsxgraph width="420px" height="300px"]] (function() { var n1 = {#num_actors#}, n2 = {#num_singers#}, per = 6; var rows = Math.ceil(n1/per) + Math.ceil(n2/per); var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-1, rows + 2.6, 10.5, -1.2], axis:false, grid:false, keepaspectratio:true, showNavigation:false, showCopyright:false, pan:{enabled:false}, zoom:{enabled:false}}); b.create('polygon', [[-0.4,-0.4],[per+0.4,-0.4],[per+0.4,rows+0.2],[-0.4,rows+0.2]], {fillColor:'#efebe9', fillOpacity:0.7, vertices:{visible:false}, borders:{strokeColor:'#8d6e63', strokeWidth:2}, fixed:true}); var row = rows - 0.5, col = 0; function put(n, colr) { for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { b.create('point', [col + 0.5, row], {name:'', size:9, fixed:true, fillColor:colr, strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); col++; if (col === per) { col = 0; row -= 1; } } if (col !== 0) { col = 0; row -= 1; } } put(n1, '#8e24aa'); put(n2, '#fb8c00'); b.create('point', [7.2, rows - 0.3], {name:'', size:7, fixed:true, fillColor:'#8e24aa', strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); b.create('text', [7.6, rows - 0.3, 'actors (' + n1 + ')'], {fontSize:13, fixed:true, anchorY:'middle'}); b.create('point', [7.2, rows - 1.3], {name:'', size:7, fixed:true, fillColor:'#fb8c00', strokeColor:'#333', showInfobox:false}); b.create('text', [7.6, rows - 1.3, 'singers (' + n2 + ')'], {fontSize:13, fixed:true, anchorY:'middle'}); b.create('text', [per/2, rows + 1.3, 'Drama club'], {fontSize:14, fixed:true, anchorX:'middle'}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

The principal randomly selects a delegation of exactly {@select_n@} students.

a) Calculate the total number of possible delegations that can be formed from the entire club.

\(n(S) =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) To find the probability of selecting at least one actor, it is easier to first find the complement: selecting no actors at all. Calculate the number of possible delegations that consist only of singers.

\(n(\text{all singers}) =\) [[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

c) Using the complement rule (\( P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{none}) \)), determine the probability that the delegation includes at least one actor.

(Enter your answer as a fully simplified fraction).

\(P(\text{at least one actor}) =\) [[input:ans3]]

[[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: The Sample Space
The club has a total of \({@num_actors@} + {@num_singers@} = {@total_pop@}\) students. We are choosing a delegation of \({@select_n@}\) students. Using the combinations formula:

\( \displaystyle n(S) = {}^{{@total_pop@}}C_{{@select_n@}} = \frac{{@total_pop@}!}{{@select_n@}!({@total_pop@} - {@select_n@})!} = {@ta1@} \)

Part b: The Complement Event
The complement of "at least one actor" is "zero actors" (meaning all \({@select_n@}\) students chosen must be singers). We calculate the combinations for choosing \({@select_n@}\) students purely from the \({@num_singers@}\) available singers:

\( \displaystyle n(\text{all singers}) = {}^{{@num_singers@}}C_{{@select_n@}} = {@ta2@} \)

Part c: The Theoretical Probability
First, we find the probability of the complement event (selecting no actors):

\( \displaystyle P(\text{all singers}) = \frac{n(\text{all singers})}{n(S)} = \frac{{@ta2@}}{{@ta1@}} \)

Then, we apply the complement rule to find our target probability:

\( \displaystyle P(\text{at least one actor}) = 1 - P(\text{all singers}) = 1 - \frac{{@ta2@}}{{@ta1@}} \)

Simplifying this mathematically yields:

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ {@ta3@} } \)

This question is based on the example Using the Complement Rule (at least one girl) in the section Theoretical Probability of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Theoretical Probability (Complement Rule)

node.description: Check absolute correctness of sample space

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully calculated the combinations for the entire sample space.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. To find the total sample space \(n(S)\), use the combinations formula \({}^nC_r\) where \(n\) is the TOTAL number of students, and \(r\) is the delegation size.

node.description: Check absolute correctness of complement combinations

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully calculated the number of ways to select only singers.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. To find the complement outcomes, calculate \({}^nC_r\) where \(n\) is specifically the number of SINGERS, and \(r\) is the delegation size.

node.description: Algebraic equivalence of final probability fraction

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You successfully applied the complement rule to find the final probability.

node.description: Check if they forgot to subtract from 1

truefeedback.text: You calculated the probability of selecting no actors. Remember to subtract this value from 1 to find the probability of selecting at least one actor.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Find the probability of the complement event (\(n(E') / n(S)\)), and then subtract it from 1.
